body.en: A matrix packs a rectangular table of numbers into one object you can add, scale, and multiply — and that algebra gives a genuinely new way to solve a linear system. This chapter builds \( 2\times2 \) matrix algebra from scratch, then pairs it with the vector tools (magnitude, dot product, angle) EST II Math Level 2 tests alongside it.
body.ar: A المصفوفة packs a rectangular الجدول of numbers into one object you can add, scale, and multiply — and that الجبر gives a genuinely new way to solve a linear system. This chapter builds \( 2\times2 \) المصفوفة الجبر from scratch, then pairs it with the المتجه tools (magnitude, dot product, الزاوية) EST II Math Level 2 tests alongside it.

label.en: ● Definition 4.1 — Matrix, addition, and scalar multiplication
label.ar: ● تعريف 4.1 — المصفوفة, addition, and scalar multiplication

body.en:
An \( m\times n \) matrix is a rectangular array of numbers with \( m \) rows and \( n \) columns. Two matrices of the same dimensions add entrywise, and a scalar \( k \) multiplies every entry:

\[ (A+B)_{ij}=a_{ij}+b_{ij}, \qquad (kA)_{ij}=k\,a_{ij}. \]
body.ar:
An \( m\times n \) matrix is a rectangular array of numbers with \( m \) rows and \( n \) columns. Two المصفوفات of the same dimensions add entrywise, and a scalar \( k \) multiplies every entry:

\[ (A+B)_{ij}=a_{ij}+b_{ij}, \qquad (kA)_{ij}=k\,a_{ij}. \]

body.en:
Let \( A=\begin{bmatrix}4&-1\\3&2\end{bmatrix} \) and \( B=\begin{bmatrix}-2&5\\1&-3\end{bmatrix} \). Find \( A+B \) and \( 2A \).

\[ A+B=\begin{bmatrix}2&4\\4&-1\end{bmatrix}, \qquad 2A=\begin{bmatrix}8&-2\\6&4\end{bmatrix}. \]
body.ar:
الشرح الرياضي (المصفوفات والمحددات والمتجهات):

Let \( A=\begin{bmatrix}4&-1\\3&2\end{bmatrix} \) and \( B=\begin{bmatrix}-2&5\\1&-3\end{bmatrix} \). Find \( A+B \) and \( 2A \).

\[ A+B=\begin{bmatrix}2&4\\4&-1\end{bmatrix}, \qquad 2A=\begin{bmatrix}8&-2\\6&4\end{bmatrix}. \]

body.en: If \( A \) is \( m\times n \) and \( B \) is \( n\times p \), the product \( AB \) is the \( m\times p \) matrix whose \( (i,j) \) entry is the dot product of row \( i \) of \( A \) with column \( j \) of \( B \): \[ (AB)_{ij}=\sum_{k=1}^{n} a_{ik}b_{kj}. \] Matrix multiplication is not commutative in general.
body.ar: If \( A \) is \( m\times n \) and \( B \) is \( n\times p \), the product \( AB \) is the \( m\times p \) المصفوفة whose \( (i,j) \) entry is the dot product of row \( i \) of \( A \) with column \( j \) of \( B \): \[ (AB)_{ij}=\sum_{k=1}^{n} a_{ik}b_{kj}. \] المصفوفة multiplication is not commutative in general.

label.en: ● Definition 4.3 — Determinant and the identity matrix
label.ar: ● تعريف 4.3 — المحدد and the المتطابقة المصفوفة

body.en: For \( A=\begin{bmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{bmatrix} \), the determinant is \( \det A=ad-bc \). The identity matrix \( I=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{bmatrix} \) satisfies \( IA=AI=A \).
body.ar: For \( A=\begin{bmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{bmatrix} \), the determinant is \( \det A=ad-bc \). The المتطابقة المصفوفة \( I=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{bmatrix} \) satisfies \( IA=AI=A \).

body.en:
If \( A=\begin{bmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{bmatrix} \) and \( \det A=ad-bc\neq0 \), then

\[ A^{-1}=\frac{1}{\det A}\begin{bmatrix}d&-b\\-c&a\end{bmatrix}. \] If \( \det A=0 \), no inverse exists.
body.ar:
الشرح الرياضي (المصفوفات والمحددات والمتجهات):

If \( A=\begin{bmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{bmatrix} \) and \( \det A=ad-bc\neq0 \), then

\[ A^{-1}=\frac{1}{\det A}\begin{bmatrix}d&-b\\-c&a\end{bmatrix}. \] If \( \det A=0 \), no inverse exists.

body.en: Let \( d_0=ad-bc\neq0 \). Multiplying \( A \) by \( \tfrac{1}{d_0}\begin{bmatrix}d&-b\\-c&a\end{bmatrix} \) gives \[ \frac{1}{d_0}\begin{bmatrix}ad-bc&-ab+ba\\cd-dc&-cb+da\end{bmatrix}=\frac{1}{d_0}\begin{bmatrix}d_0&0\\0&d_0\end{bmatrix}=I, \] and the same computation in the other order also gives \( I \), so this is a genuine two-sided inverse. If \( \det A=0 \) and some \( B \) satisfied \( AB=I \), then \( \det A\cdot\det B=\det(AB)=\det I=1 \) — impossible since the left side is \( 0 \). So no inverse exists. \( \blacksquare \)
body.ar:
الشرح الرياضي (المصفوفات والمحددات والمتجهات):

Let \( d_0=ad-bc\neq0 \). Multiplying \( A \) by \( \tfrac{1}{d_0}\begin{bmatrix}d&-b\\-c&a\end{bmatrix} \) gives \[ \frac{1}{d_0}\begin{bmatrix}ad-bc&-ab+ba\\cd-dc&-cb+da\end{bmatrix}=\frac{1}{d_0}\begin{bmatrix}d_0&0\\0&d_0\end{bmatrix}=I, \] and the same computation in the other order also gives \( I \), so this is a genuine two-sided inverse. If \( \det A=0 \) and some \( B \) satisfied \( AB=I \), then \( \det A\cdot\det B=\det(AB)=\det I=1 \) — impossible since the left side is \( 0 \). So no inverse exists. \( \blacksquare \)

label.en: Worked example 4.C — Invert a matrix and solve a system with it
label.ar: مثال محلول 4.C — Invert a المصفوفة and solve a system with it

body.ar:
الشرح الرياضي (المصفوفات والمحددات والمتجهات):

Solve \( \begin{cases}4x+y=14\\3x+2y=13\end{cases} \) using \( \mathbf{x}=A^{-1}\mathbf{b} \).

\( A=\begin{bmatrix}4&1\\3&2\end{bmatrix} \), \( \det A=(4)(2)-(1)(3)=5 \), so \[ A^{-1}=\frac{1}{5}\begin{bmatrix}2&-1\\-3&4\end{bmatrix}. \]

\[ x=\tfrac{1}{5}\big(2(14)-1(13)\big)=\tfrac{15}{5}=3, \qquad y=\tfrac{1}{5}\big(-3(14)+4(13)\big)=\tfrac{10}{5}=2. \] Check: \( 4(3)+2=14 \) ✓ and \( 3(3)+2(2)=13 \) ✓.

label.en: ● Definition 4.4 — Vectors: magnitude and dot product
label.ar: ● تعريف 4.4 — المتجهات: magnitude and dot product

body.en: A vector \( \mathbf{u}=\langle u_1,u_2\rangle \) has magnitude \( |\mathbf{u}|=\sqrt{u_1^2+u_2^2} \). The dot product of \( \mathbf{u} \) and \( \mathbf{v}=\langle v_1,v_2\rangle \) is \( \mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}=u_1v_1+u_2v_2 \).
body.ar: A المتجه \( \mathbf{u}=\langle u_1,u_2\rangle \) has magnitude \( |\mathbf{u}|=\sqrt{u_1^2+u_2^2} \). The dot product of \( \mathbf{u} \) and \( \mathbf{v}=\langle v_1,v_2\rangle \) is \( \mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}=u_1v_1+u_2v_2 \).

body.en: For nonzero vectors with angle \( \theta \) between them, \[ \cos\theta=\frac{\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}}{|\mathbf{u}|\,|\mathbf{v}|}. \]
body.ar: For nonzero المتجهات with الزاوية \( \theta \) between them, \[ \cos\theta=\frac{\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}}{|\mathbf{u}|\,|\mathbf{v}|}. \]

body.en: Placing \( \mathbf{u},\mathbf{v} \) tail-to-tail, the Law of Cosines on the triangle with sides \( |\mathbf{u}|,|\mathbf{v}|,|\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}| \) gives \( |\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}|^2=|\mathbf{u}|^2+|\mathbf{v}|^2-2|\mathbf{u}||\mathbf{v}|\cos\theta \). Expanding the left side as \( (\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u})\cdot(\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u})=|\mathbf{v}|^2-2\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}+|\mathbf{u}|^2 \) and equating the two expressions cancels \( |\mathbf{u}|^2+|\mathbf{v}|^2 \), leaving \( -2\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}=-2|\mathbf{u}||\mathbf{v}|\cos\theta \), i.e. \( \cos\theta=\dfrac{\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}}{|\mathbf{u}||\mathbf{v}|} \). \( \blacksquare \)
body.ar: Placing \( \mathbf{u},\mathbf{v} \) tail-to-tail, the Law of Cosines on the المثلث with sides \( |\mathbf{u}|,|\mathbf{v}|,|\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}| \) gives \( |\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}|^2=|\mathbf{u}|^2+|\mathbf{v}|^2-2|\mathbf{u}||\mathbf{v}|\cos\theta \). Expanding the left side as \( (\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u})\cdot(\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u})=|\mathbf{v}|^2-2\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}+|\mathbf{u}|^2 \) and equating the two expressions cancels \( |\mathbf{u}|^2+|\mathbf{v}|^2 \), leaving \( -2\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}=-2|\mathbf{u}||\mathbf{v}|\cos\theta \), i.e. \( \cos\theta=\dfrac{\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}}{|\mathbf{u}||\mathbf{v}|} \). \( \blacksquare \)

body.en:
Matrix Multiplication Dimension Mismatch: An \(m \times k\) matrix can only multiply a \(k \times n\) matrix; the result is \(m \times n\). Multiplication is strictly non-commutative (\(AB \neq BA\)).

Inverse Formula Sign Errors: In \(A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{ad - bc}\begin{pmatrix}d & -b\\ -c & a\end{pmatrix}\), note that the main diagonal entries \(a\) and \(d\) swap positions without sign change, while off-diagonal entries \(b\) and \(c\) change signs without swapping.

Perpendicular vs Parallel Vectors: \(\mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{v} = 0\) means the vectors are perpendicular (orthogonal). If \(\mathbf{u} = k\mathbf{v}\), they are parallel.
body.ar:

Inverse الصيغة Sign Errors: In \(A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{ad - bc}\begin{pmatrix}d & -b\\ -c & a\end{pmatrix}\), note that the main diagonal entries \(a\) and \(d\) swap positions without sign change, while off-diagonal entries \(b\) and \(c\) change signs without swapping.

Perpendicular vs Parallel المتجهات: \(\mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{v} = 0\) means the المتجهات are perpendicular (orthogonal). If \(\mathbf{u} = k\mathbf{v}\), they are parallel.

question.en: Let \(A = \begin{pmatrix}4 & 3\\ 2 & 2\end{pmatrix}\). Find \(A^{-1}\) and compute the vector \(\mathbf{x} = A^{-1}\begin{pmatrix}10\\ 6\end{pmatrix}\).
question.ar: ليكن \(A = \begin{pmatrix}4 & 3\\ 2 & 2\end{pmatrix}\). أوجد \(A^{-1}\) and compute the vector \(\mathbf{x} = A^{-1}\begin{pmatrix}10\\ 6\end{pmatrix}\).

solution.ar:
خطوات الحل التفصيلية: 1. Compute \(\det(A) = (4)(2) - (3)(2) = 8 - 6 = 2\).
2. Form \(A^{-1}\): \[ A^{-1} = \frac{1}{2}\begin{pmatrix}2 & -3\\ -2 & 4\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}1 & -1.5\\ -1 & 2\end{pmatrix}. \]
3. Multiply by \(\begin{pmatrix}10\\ 6\end{pmatrix}\): \[ \mathbf{x} = \frac{1}{2}\begin{pmatrix}2(10) + (-3)(6)\\ -2(10) + 4(6)\end{pmatrix} = \frac{1}{2}\begin{pmatrix}20 - 18\\ -20 + 24\end{pmatrix} = \frac{1}{2}\begin{pmatrix}2\\ 4\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}1\\ 2\end{pmatrix}. \]

hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(\det(A) = (4)(2) - (3)(2) = 8 - 6\) لتبسيط الخطوة.
تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(A^{-1}\) ، \(A^{-1} = \frac{1}{2}\begin{pmatrix}2 & -3\\ -2 & 4\end{pmatrix}\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(\begin{pmatrix}10\\ 6\end{pmatrix}\) ، \(x = \frac{1}{2}\begin{pmatrix}2(10) + (-3)(6)\\ -2(10) + 4(6)\end{pmatrix} = \frac{1}{2}\begin{pmatrix}20 - 18\\ -20 + 24\end{pmatrix} = \frac{1}{2}\begin{pmatrix}2\\ 4\end{pmatrix}\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

question.en: [Practice 2 · Hard] A linear transformation in the 2D plane is represented by the matrix \( M = \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix} \). This transformation maps the point \( P(1, 2) \) to \( P'(-3, 7) \) and the point \( Q(3, 1) \) to \( Q'(5, 1) \). Determine the values of \( a, b, c, \) and \( d \), and then calculate the sum \( a+b+c+d \).
question.ar: [Practice 2 · Hard] A linear transformation in the 2D plane is represented بتطبيق matrix \( M = \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix} \). This transformation maps the point \( P(1, 2) \) to \( P'(-3, 7) \) and the point \( Q(3, 1) \) to \( Q'(5, 1) \). حدّد values of \( a, b, c, \) and \( d \), and then احسب sum \( a+b+c+d \).

hints.en: Let the linear transformation matrix be \( M = \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix} \).
hints.ar: ليكن the linear transformation matrix be \( M = \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix} \).
أعد كتابة العلاقة وبسّطها للحصول على: \( -5a = 4 - 14 \).

hints.en: The sum of the elements of the transformation matrix is \(a + b + c + d = 2 + 1 + 3 + 3\).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(a + b + c + d = 2 + 1 + 3 + 3\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

solution.en:
Let the linear transformation matrix be \( M = \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix} \). 

The transformation of a point \( \mathbf{x} \) to \( \mathbf{x'} \) is given by \( M\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{x'} \). 

For point \( P(1, 2) \) mapped to \( P'(4, 9) \): 
\[ \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 9 \end{pmatrix} \] 
This yields the equations: 
1) \( a + 2b = 4 \) 
2) \( c + 2d = 9 \)

For point \( Q(3, 1) \) mapped to \( Q'(7, 12) \): 
\[ \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 7 \\ 12 \end{pmatrix} \] 
This yields the equations: 
3) \( 3a + b = 7 \) 
4) \( 3c + d = 12 \)

We need to solve these two systems of linear equations for \( a, b, c, \) and \( d \). 

Solving for \( a \) and \( b \) using equations (1) and (3):
From equation (3), \( b = 7 - 3a \). Substitute this into equation (1):
\( a + 2(7 - 3a) = 4 \)
\( a + 14 - 6a = 4 \)
\( -5a = 4 - 14 \)
\( -5a = -10 \)
\( a = 2 \)

Now substitute the value of \( a \) back into the expression for \( b \):
\( b = 7 - 3(2) = 7 - 6 = 1 \)

Solving for \( c \) and \( d \) using equations (2) and (4):
From equation (4), \( d = 12 - 3c \). Substitute this into equation (2):
\( c + 2(12 - 3c) = 9 \)
\( c + 24 - 6c = 9 \)
\( -5c = 9 - 24 \)
\( -5c = -15 \)
\( c = 3 \)

Now substitute the value of \( c \) back into the expression for \( d \):
\( d = 12 - 3(3) = 12 - 9 = 3 \)

So, the transformation matrix is \( M = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 3 & 3 \end{pmatrix} \). 

The sum of the elements of the transformation matrix is \( a + b + c + d = 2 + 1 + 3 + 3 = 9 \). 

Common misconceptions might arise from errors in solving the systems of equations, such as sign errors or algebraic mistakes when isolating variables. For instance, incorrectly solving for \( b \) or \( d \) could lead to a wrong sum. Alternatively, a student might forget to sum all four elements and only sum the elements of one row or column.

ليكن the linear transformation matrix be \( M = \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix} \). 

The transformation of a point \( \mathbf{x} \) to \( \mathbf{x'} \) is given by \( M\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{x'} \). 

For point \( P(1, 2) \) mapped to \( P'(4, 9) \): 
\[ \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 9 \end{pmatrix} \] 
This yields the equations: 
1) \( a + 2b = 4 \) 
2) \( c + 2d = 9 \)

For point \( Q(3, 1) \) mapped to \( Q'(7, 12) \): 
\[ \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 7 \\ 12 \end{pmatrix} \] 
This yields the equations: 
3) \( 3a + b = 7 \) 
4) \( 3c + d = 12 \)

We need to حل these two systems of linear equations for \( a, b, c, \) and \( d \). 

Solving for \( a \) and \( b \) using equations (1) and (3):
From equation (3), \( b = 7 - 3a \). عوّض this into equation (1):
\( a + 2(7 - 3a) = 4 \)
\( a + 14 - 6a = 4 \)
\( -5a = 4 - 14 \)
\( -5a = -10 \)
\( a = 2 \)

Now عوّض the value of \( a \) back into the expression for \( b \):
\( b = 7 - 3(2) = 7 - 6 = 1 \)

Solving for \( c \) and \( d \) using equations (2) and (4):
From equation (4), \( d = 12 - 3c \). عوّض this into equation (2):
\( c + 2(12 - 3c) = 9 \)
\( c + 24 - 6c = 9 \)
\( -5c = 9 - 24 \)
\( -5c = -15 \)
\( c = 3 \)

Now عوّض the value of \( c \) back into the expression for \( d \):
\( d = 12 - 3(3) = 12 - 9 = 3 \)

So, the transformation matrix is \( M = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 3 & 3 \end{pmatrix} \). 

The sum of the elements of the transformation matrix is \( a + b + c + d = 2 + 1 + 3 + 3 = 9 \).

For instance, incorrectly solving for \( b \) or \( d \) could lead to a wrong sum. Alternatively, a student might forget to sum all four elements and only sum the elements of one row or column.

question.en: [Practice 4 · Medium] A translation maps point \( A(1, 2) \) to \( A'(-4, 2) \) and point \( B(3, 5) \) to \( B'(-2, 5) \). This transformation is represented by \( \begin{pmatrix} x' \\ y' \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix} a \\ b \end{pmatrix} \). Find the values of \( a \) and \( b \).
question.ar: [Practice 4 · Medium] A translation maps point \( A(1, 2) \) to \( A'(-4, 2) \) and point \( B(3, 5) \) to \( B'(-2, 5) \). This transformation is represented by \( \begin{pmatrix} x' \\ y' \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix} a \\ b \end{pmatrix} \). أوجد values of \( a \) and \( b \).

hints.en: Subtracting the original coordinates of \( A(1, 2) \) from its image \( A'(-4, 2) \) gives the translation vector: \(\begin{pmatrix} a \\ b \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -4 - 1 \\ 2 - 2 \end{pmatrix}\).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \( A(1, 2) \) ، \( A'(-4, 2) \) ، \(\begin{pmatrix} a \\ b \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -4 - 1 \\ 2 - 2 \end{pmatrix}\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: Checking with \( B(3, 5) \to B'(-2, 5) \) confirms. Set up the numerical expression: \((-2 - 3, 5 - 5)\).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \( B(3, 5) \to B'(-2, 5) \) ، \((-2 - 3, 5 - 5)\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: Evaluate \((-2 - 3, 5 - 5)\) step by step to obtain the final answer.
hints.ar: احسب قيمة \((-2 - 3, 5 - 5)\) step by step to obtain the final answer.

solution.en:
Subtracting the original coordinates of \( A(1, 2) \) from its image \( A'(-4, 2) \) gives the translation vector:
\[ \begin{pmatrix} a \\ b \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -4 - 1 \\ 2 - 2 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -5 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}. \]
Checking with \( B(3, 5) \to B'(-2, 5) \) confirms \( (-2 - 3, 5 - 5) = (-5, 0) \). Thus, \( a = -5 \) and \( b = 0 \).
